title: Anthropic Signs $10 Billion Cloud Deal With Norwegian Startup Volta, Backed by Nvidia's Latest Chips
excerpt: The six-year compute agreement will see crypto-mining partner Bitdeer help build a 133-megawatt data centre in Norway powered by Nvidia's Vera Rubin architecture.
body:
• Anthropic has reportedly signed a $10 billion, six-year cloud compute deal with AI startup Volta, according to Bloomberg.
  • Volta, founded earlier in 2026 and part of Nvidia's Cloud Partner program, will build a 133-megawatt data centre in Norway using Nvidia's state-of-the-art Vera Rubin chip architecture.
  • Crypto-mining company Bitdeer will partner with Volta to develop the facility, marking another convergence of crypto infrastructure and AI compute demand.
  • The deal follows recent Anthropic compute partnerships with SpaceX and Amazon as the Claude maker aggressively scales capacity to compete with OpenAI and Google.

Anthropic is pouring another $10 billion into its compute buildout, this time through a deal with Volta, a fledgling AI cloud startup that will provide the Claude maker with dedicated capacity over six years.

The Deal

Bloomberg first reported the agreement on Tuesday, citing anonymous sources familiar with the transaction. Volta, founded earlier this year, will deliver cloud compute from a new data centre in Norway with a 133-megawatt capacity. The facility will run on Nvidia's Vera Rubin systems — the chipmaker's latest and most powerful AI chip architecture, which represents a generational leap beyond the current Blackwell platform.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Ob5NiR-BkQ4

Volta is part of Nvidia's Cloud Partner program, a consortium of AI infrastructure providers that use Nvidia GPUs in their data centres. The startup had previously spoken publicly about a deal with an unnamed AI lab but hadn't identified the specific company until Bloomberg's report.

The Crypto Connection

The deal has an unusual partner: Bitdeer, a crypto-mining company that will help develop the Norwegian data centre. The involvement of a crypto firm underscores a growing trend — as cryptocurrency mining profitability fluctuates, mining companies are pivoting their infrastructure expertise and power procurement capabilities toward AI workloads, where demand for compute is virtually insatiable.

Norway's appeal is straightforward. Cheap hydroelectric power, cool climate that reduces cooling costs, and political stability make it an attractive location for power-hungry AI data centres. Several hyperscalers have already established Nordic operations for similar reasons.

Anthropic's Compute Arms Race

The Volta deal is the latest in a string of aggressive infrastructure moves by Anthropic as it wages a corporate battle with OpenAI, Google DeepMind, and Meta's AI division. The company recently announced compute deals with SpaceX and expanded its existing partnership with Amazon, which has invested billions in the startup and provides capacity through AWS.

"Anthropic has sought to aggressively expand its compute capacity over the last several months as it wages a corporate battle with its competitors."

— TechCrunch

The scale of spending is staggering. A single $10 billion deal from a company that was valued at roughly $60 billion in its last funding round speaks to how capital-intensive frontier AI has become. Training and serving models at the scale Anthropic operates requires thousands of cutting-edge GPUs running continuously, and securing guaranteed access to that hardware is now as much a competitive moat as the models themselves.

What It Means

For the broader AI industry, the deal signals that compute scarcity will remain a defining constraint. Companies that can lock in long-term supply agreements — even at eye-watering prices — gain a structural advantage over competitors still scrambling for GPU allocations on the spot market. It also validates the emerging category of dedicated AI cloud providers, which sit between the hyperscalers and the AI labs themselves.
